accepted.question_text: Does there exist an entire function f(z) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n z^n such that every coefficient a_n is a hypergeometric term over the rational numbers, meaning that a_{n+1}/a_n is a rational function of n and the coefficients defining the term are rational, and such that evaluating the function at z = 1 gives f(1) = π? Equivalently, can π be represented by a hypergeometric rational-coefficient series that converges superexponentially fast rather than merely exponentially fast?

evidence.quote: Does there exist an entire function f(z) = P n≥0 anz^n such that the coefficients an are hypergeometric terms over the rational numbers, and f(1) = π?
But can it be 0? That is, can such a series converge superexponentially fast?

accepted.question_text: Can one choose a set S of positive integers and a set M of nonnegative integers containing 0 such that both S and M are infinite, every sufficiently large integer n has at least one partition counted by p(S, M; n), where p(S, M; n) denotes the number of partitions of n whose parts all lie in S and whose multiplicities all lie in M, and the counting function p(S, M; n) grows at most polynomially in n?

evidence.quote: Let S be a set of positive integers and let M be a set of nonnegative integers containing 0. Let p(S, M; n) denote the number of partitions of n whose parts all lie in S and the multiplicities of whose parts all lie in M.
Can we choose S and M so that 1. S and M are both infinite sets, and 2. all sufficiently large integers n are represented, i.e., p(S, M; n) > 0 for all large n,
3. p(S, M; n) is of at most polynomial growth in n?

accepted.question_text: Let f(z) = arctan(√(2e^{-z} − 1)) / √(2e^{-z} − 1), and write its power-series expansion as f(z) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n z^n. Determine the first term in the asymptotic behavior of the coefficients a_n.

evidence.quote: If f(z) = P n≥0 anz^n, find the first term of the asymptotic behavior of the an’s.
Recent progress: Mark Ward has found [1] a complete expansion of these coefficients.

accepted.question_text: Call an integer n p-balanced if, among the nonzero binomial coefficients (n choose k) modulo a prime p for 0 ≤ k ≤ n, the quadratic residues modulo p and the quadratic nonresidues modulo p occur equally often. Call a prime p special if no integer n with 0 ≤ n < p is p-balanced. The primes 2, 3, and 11 are known to be special, and no other primes below 1,000,000 are special. Are there any additional special primes?

evidence.quote: An integer n is p-balanced if, among the nonzero values of {( n k )}^n_{k=0} (mod p) there are equal numbers of quadratic residues and quadratic nonresidues mod p.
Say that the prime p is special if no integer n, 0 ≤ n < p is p-balanced. The primes 2, 3, 11 are special, and no other primes < 1, 000, 000 are special.
Are there any more special primes?

accepted.question_text: Let k be an even integer. Let y_k(n) denote the number of standard Young tableaux with n cells whose first row has length at most k, and let u_k(n) denote the number of permutations of n letters whose longest ascending subsequence has length at most k. Wilf states the finite relation (2n choose n)u_k(n) = Σ_r (2n choose r)(−1)^r y_k(r)y_k(2n − r). Find a purely combinatorial derivation of this identity, rather than an analytic derivation.

evidence.quote: More precisely, let k be an even number, let yk(n) be the number of Young tableaux of n cells whose first row has length ≤ k, and let uk(n) be the number of permutations of n letters that have no ascending subsequence of length > k. Then it is true that (2n n) uk(n) = Σ_r (2n r) (−1)^r yk(r)yk(2n − r).
That being the case, it should have a purely combinatorial derivation. Find one.

accepted.question_text: Let T(n) be the set of partitions of n for which the nonzero multiplicities of the parts are all distinct, and let f(n) = |T(n)|. Prove any interesting theorems about the function f(n).

evidence.quote: Let T (n) be the set of partitions of n for which the (nonzero) multiplicities of its parts are all different, and write f(n) = |T (n)|.
Find any interesting theorems about f(n).

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) be the number of monomials that appear in the expansion of the n × n general Toeplitz determinant det(a_|i−j|)_{i,j=1,...,n}. Determine f(n). In addition, decide whether f(n) has superexponential growth.

evidence.quote: Find f(n), the number of monomials in the expansion of the n × n general Toeplitz determinant det ( a|i−j| )_{i,j=1,...,n}.

accepted.question_text: For which graphs G does equality hold in the bound χ(G) ≤ 1 + max_{G'⊆G} δ(G'), where χ(G) is the chromatic number and δ(G') is the minimum degree of the subgraph G'? In other words, characterize exactly the graphs for which the chromatic number equals one plus the maximum, over all subgraphs G' of G, of the minimum degree of G'.
accepted.context_brief: Equality cases for a chromatic-number bound

evidence.quote: By a theorem of the late George Szekeres and myself, we have χ(G) ≤ 1 + max_{G′⊆G} δ(G′), where χ is the chromatic number and δ is the minimum degree of the vertices.
For precisely which graphs G does the sign of equality hold?
